title: Warner Bros. Studio Harry Potter Tour with Superior Transport from London
description: Secure your admission ticket in advance, avoid the hassle of driving in London traffic, and go behind the scenes of the making of Harry Potter with this wizarding world–themed Warner Bros. Studio Tour London package. With this experience, relax on a plush coach on the way to the studios, and spend time independently exploring Harry Potter film sets. Plus, see props and costumes featured in the popular movies.

placeList.title: Warner Bros. Studio Tour London - The Making of Harry Potter

reviews.usertext:
Visited here for second time in ten years and things have changed quite a lot. Firstly parking is good and there were no queues at the entrance . The tour is very good and we really enjoyed this again . The only downside was the backlot cafe which is needed as it’s about an hour or so into the tour. The queues for food and butter beer was bad and the service was painfully slow. This area needs sorting out and the prices for food and especially butter beer is extortionate. Butter beer is 6-95 with a souvenir plastic cup but it’s way too much for essentially cream
Soda and extracts . There needs to be other food or drink outlets throughout to alleviate the queues at this cafe. All in all the tour is very good , bit pricey but worth at least one visit .

First let me say that Evan Evans Tours are great. We took 2 Evan Evans Tours when we visited London, both bus trips, guides and drivers were excellent. When you visit the Making of Harry Potter via the tour company, once you arrive at the studios, you are given a large block of time for your visit, like 4-4 1/2 hours. This is great if you are a huge Harry Potter fan, because there is a lot to see and all of the sets, props, costumes, art, etc. is amazing. But if you're just a mild enthusiast like us, you will finish the tour in a hour and a half, two hours max. That left us with over 2 hours until the bus was schedule to return to London. The tour company does provide you with instructions to make your way back using public transportation but at your own cost, which we did (shuttle>train>tube>walk) and there were no issues. I say all this to say the Making of Harry Potter attraction is great, I recommend if you are a fan. But if you don't see yourself staying for 4-4 1/2 hours, arrange your own transportation. It's really easy to get there. I highly recommend Evans Evans tours, they take care of everything, just be aware the transportation time table is fixed.

The studio was incredible and we wished we had twice as much time there. This booking is basically for a bus ride from London to the studio and back, and then the ticket to enter once you get there. The bus was nice and had USB chargers for each seat…and left right on time. The guy handing out entry tickets when we got there seemed kind of lost and people were getting a little annoyed since they were anxious to go inside, but other than that, was great. The studio experience was next level and a must for Harry Potter fans.

The bus takes over an hour to get you there is is packed and uncomfortable. By the time we got there received our tickets and got through security we had exactly 3.5 hours to see the entire exhibit and grab lunch. It takes 20 to 30 minutes to get to where the tour actually begins and they tell you the two sections take 1.5 hours each but that depends on the crowds. The day I went there were a ton of school kids. After completing the first section I had only an hour left before I would have to get to the bus. I decided to each lunch and take the train back to my hotel, which was needed because i needed an extra hour.

It is cheaper to buy your tickets on Warner bros site and take the train from London. there is a free shuttle from the train station to Warner bros, it is easy and there is staff in the train station at Victoria to show you where to go.

I had the best 6th month anniversary with my boyfriend at Harry potter world. It was amazing to see the different sets that the characters performed on: it was my first time there and I loved it. I really would like to go again and I would recommend it to anyone who likes Harry potter or doesn't know much about it as it is fun for all the family.

The attraction is really good and the staff are very well trained at enhancing the experience.

There was a few issues for me, a lot of the displays would be better if you could walk through them, like the train and the night bus etc. Also as the tickets are expensive it is quite bad how much they charge for film snippets and photos. The site is cleverly set out to make money so that you have to walk through both the cafe and shop? Both of which are extortionate!!!!

This was a great tour. It was easy to find Evan Evans tour company office as we happened to be staying in a hotel that was walking distance away. However, you can easily get there by foot from victoria train/bus station. The bus rides to and from the studio were comfortable and on time even with the traffic we experienced in London that day. As for the attraction itself, the Harry Potter studio tour was phenomenal! I would definitely recommend it to any Harry Potter fan as it was one of the highlights of my trip to the UK. I would recommend not wasting time in the cafeteria (unless you want a quick butterbeer) as you only have about 3 hours if you do a bus tour (of course you could spend as much time as you want at the studio tour if you had your own means of travel). However, my brother and I had the best time seeing so many real sets and props, learning about visual/special effects, and enjoying the magic that the HP world encompasses. I will always remember this experience, and would rate it even more immersive than HP world in Universal Studios, Florida. I can't recommend the HP studio tour enough! Great for the whole family or any Harry Potter fan, really!

This tour is all about the bus, as the Harry Potter tickets are the same ones you can buy directly. Our bus was not "superior" as promised, had no wifi as promised and had no USB charging as promised. So basically not what we were promised. A very expensive bus ride that didn't deliver. Recent reviews suggest this is happening quite a bit with this company. Will dispute my credit card charge.

evan evan gives a wrong address, they pass the post code from the contiki agency and when I got there they informed me that I was supposed to wait there for the bus to come. No bus showed up, the bus leaves in front of a cafe nearby and went without me and my friend, I called them and everything and now they play dead and refuse to refund. Rude and unprofessional people who know how to pass a correct post code.

Took Granddaughter age 12 in Feb 2022 was her Xmas present.
Great experience for her in lots of ways.
Would do it differently now I know more about it
1. Golden tours bus was not a good experience, had to travel to bus stop at Baker Street early am, cost of taxi. Stood 30 mins in cold. Couldn’t hear sound on film. Long journey cost £70 for 1 adult 1 child.
Arrived hour prior to appointed entry time, did get in earlier but obviously Finished tour 2 hrs prior to bus journey back to London.
So… got free bus to Watford, took 22 mins on train from there to Euston station near our hotel. Cost £12 we were back in our hotel 2 hrs earlier than expected. Much better experience for us both.
She loved HP experience the staff, the facilities and the tour were fantastic great interaction definitely made up for the bus journey.
The cafe was poor choice of food not the best so would take picnic if I ever returned.
Overall a great day.

Having this tour was a good idea as it took out worrying about transportation to the studio. Just remember that the studio is pretty big with a lot to see and do so make sure you pay attention to time so you don’t hold up the bus when it’s time to leave. Also factor in lines for photos, gift shop, food, etc.

Incredible to see so many original costumes and sets, highly recommended. The food was a big disappointment though, bought two vegan hot dogs and they were so dry and tasteless we could hardly swallow them, heard the same thing about the meat ones too. The butterbeer was fantastic though. A great experience overall.

I was at first worried about being in a confined space for the first time with lots of people, but I hadn’t needed to worry. The whole set up is fantastic lots of sanitiser stations at all touch points, reduced numbers compared to my last visit. Felt at ease the whole way round staff so helpful as I wasn’t feeling to good nothing a problem. The whole experience was amazing well done.

We’ve never been to London and this cut out the stress of figuring out transportation. Our ride there was shorter than expected- we were almost an hour early but were allowed admission, so that was awesome. We had plenty of time to explore. However, coming back to Kings Cross around 5pm took well over an hour (and the bus was very hot). The pickup location at Kings Cross is very convenient especially if you’re staying at a hotel.

The service provided by Evans Evans was really good, the bus left on time and spared me from a possible stressful trip with public transportation. However they just offer us 4 hours inside the Studios and this is not enough! The place is huge and with so many things to do/see. At the end of the tour I had to rush a little bit so I wouldn’t miss the bus. I would say at least make it 5 hours and see what people will say.
Great visit, would recommend even if your not the biggest Harry Potter fan like myself. Amazing tour. Lasted for us around 2hr 45min. Merchandise is extremely expensive (£10 for a keyring)

Visiting the studio itself is awesome! This "tour" is simply a bus (transportation) to the studio and a ticket. The bus driver did not say a word the entire hour there or back. Did not point out sights we passed, or say a word about Harry Potter. There was a tv at the front of the bus and he played another unrelated movie with no sound, when he could have easily played Harry Potter and everyone would have been happy. Bus did not have wifi either. If I went again, I would simply buy tickets to the studio and find my own transportation, because it is very hard to see everything in the few hours they give you before the bus leaves.

What a day. Travelled from Dublin for the day.
Flew Ryanair to Luton Airport (33 euro pp) at 8am, private taxi ordered in advance to pick us up at 10:30 (200 euro return) and drop us back at 4:30 then flew home at 8pm.
3 adults, 6 kids ages 10-13.
A great day had by all. Very interesting and great fun from beginning to end. The great hall is amazing, all laid out for a feast!
There are lots of opportunities for photos and the butter beer was delish!
It takes about 4 hours to get through everything.
Lots of places to buy snacks on the way around and places to sit and have a picnic if you bring your own. If you like Harry Potter, it's well worth a visit.
Gift shop is a bit pricey so be prepared...

My girlfriend and I visited the studios at the beginning of February, and the entire experience definitely exceeded expectations. The amount of props from each film is staggering, and I was definitely surprised by the number of life size sets that were still intact.

Only downside is that all of the souvenirs are on the expensive side, but that definitely doesn't detract from an amazing experience. Would definitely recommend!

The tour was well organised - important in freezing weather. We were in a small group, we had a knowledgeable young guide (possibly a trained actress?) who is obviously passionate about Harry Potter, and who kept on giving us the "inside story." My granddaughter (14) said it was the highlight of an extensive 2-week trip of England.

We left 15minutes late from London because we waited for some late people.
It was asked to be at 6:50pm at the bus outside the HP Studio and that the bus would leave at 7pm.
I arrived outside at 7:01pm, and saw the bus drove away!!!
It could have waited for me 1 more freaking minute...

Amazing! It's the only thing to say! The staff were all.amazing there was a Lady called Emily T that was in the props room she was wonderful and very informative. There was also a gentleman called Lee who was on Diagon Alley, He not only knew all his facts he was also a charismatic storyteller. Fantastic man. There was one other that stood out and that was Hope, in the castle model room. She spent a lot of time talking to my daughter and giving her loads of information. Thank you, It was an amazing trip x

We had a great and comfortable time traveling on the bus back and forth from the WB Studio: The Making of Harry Potter. The bus was clean, seats comfortable, and had charging ports. Our bus driver played one of the HP movies for us to keep us entertained while we are aboard. There's no toilet on the bus so the tour company staff will tell you to use the toilet before getting on the bus. It's about an hour to hour and a half to the destination. They provide you with paper tickets to enter the studio. Once you get there, you have 4 hours to view on your own leisure. We were originally planning on a trip to the studio by ourselves but saw that regular tickets were totally sold out for the month and we weren't sure about our ride options, which is why we chose to go with Evan Evans Tours. We are glad we did because the ride was comfortable and they gave us enough time to look around. Would probably try one of their London tours next time we are back.

Though we had a lovely day the bugging of the tour was rushed and cramped.they cramed 150 into a room and rushed us straight out the another room with chairs where after searing for 10 mins rushed us out telling us come on we need to get the screen back down, once in the big hall then rushed us to the front of the hall unable to see the displays and spoke without a mic so we couldn't hear as we had 2 young children and we were pushed to the back we missed it all then told us to vacate the big hall for the next four telling us we could go back after well we couldn't. After that we walked around on our own and it was fantastic so much to see and read no doubt we missed alot. If you are visiting take a pack lunch (a hotdog is £9) and be prepared for lots of add ons 4 places for pictures at £15 a picture ends up very costly and hi for the early tour to much to see in a few hours. Lovely place and amazing how they done things.

I took my 7 year old daughter who is starting to get into Harry Potter. It was 100% magical, not overly busy when we went in the evening. Be prepared for the high prices in the gift shop if you're taking fans! The cafe food was fine, not overly expensive. There is a cafe at the entrance and then halfway through. My daughter loved the interactive wand lesson. We are now watching the films again to spot what we have seen in person. Loved it 10/10

Absolutely fantastic experience for Harry potter fans and would be film makers. Awesome to see how everything is made and filmed.
The only negative experience of our visit was the diagon alley portion of the tour. It looked incredible, like right out of the movie, with the cobbled street winding up through the shops. However it's cobbled street was almost impossible to pass for the wheelchair users in our group. I recommend an alternate, smoother route that would negate pain and discomfort.
Other than that it's brilliant.

Great motorcoach transportation with friendly driver. The exhibit itself was AMAZING! The first two sections have behind the scenes info with guides and then you are released on your own to go through the sets. Far too many things to describe but it is all spectacular, you feel like you are in the grand hall, sit inside Hagrid's motorcycle,use magic to lift a broom, etc.

Amazing visit that was supposed to last half a day turned into a whole day great visit. We are not the biggest fans of Harry Potter moviies, we just like them but this tour was amazing, interesting, there are soo many things to see and do, for kids and for grown ups. Tour guides were great and very informative.. after the tour ended we were able to come back in and explore a bit more, que in for pictures. It was an amazing day.

It is an splendid and worthwhile place to visit. You will be excited if you are Harry Potter fans. Even if you are not, you still need to come as there was many different plots to see. If you travel by riound trip transportation bus, you would find time (stay 4 hours) is limited. If you could hire a cab to and from if you are Harry Potter fans.

I loved this place. The ride in the bus was fun because the driver talked to us before we left (thank you E and E tours).

The staff in Warner Bros. Studio there is so much you can say they are so nice, friendly and helpful. They explained things when you couldn't figure out how to do and always made my son laugh.

The place was so clean and tidy. With everything going on with the covid virus then made sure everyone was safe as well as happy.

If your every in London this is a must see stop even if its just the once.

Now I don't want to give away much but my favourite part was the break in at the bank.

Such an amazing day out! So many things to see and explore. My autistic son was so excited but I worried about the crowds being too much, the sensory room is an amazing addition to the tour. A massive Thank you to Troy D and Niamh M in the shop, my son was very overwhelmed by choosing a wand in the shop, they helped him choose the perfect wand for him. Amazing team work by both and so considerate of my sons situation! Thank you both

Booked the WB studio tour, via Expedia. Evan Evans confirmed our tour, took our payment, then cancelled our booking just days before our tour. Our 9-yr son was so disappointed. We planned so much of our trip around it. And Evan Evans was not very helpful with the refund. And barely apologetic. And no explanation as to the reason for the cancellation. We had to reach out to Expedia ourselves, and while on hold, our Expedia agent had to “convince” the agency to give us a refund after they offered us an alternate tour date, 3 days after we were scheduled to leave London. So, a completely useless option. I’m sure the tour would have been fun if Evan Evans honored their booking.

Be very careful when booking with Evan Evans Travel.

Very great tour for anyone who loves Harry Potter and the magic of film! They gave us a little over 4 hours to do the tour. I took my time with the exhibit and at a meal in a little under three hours. I feel like cutting about 30 minutes from the excursion time would be a good compromise.

We enjoyed not having to find tickets or transportation to the Warner Bros. Studio. Evan Evans transports you there, gives you your ticket and away you go. We had 4 hours (plenty of time for our family of 4) to explore and eat dinner. Then we had a nice ride back to London.

I was a HP fan before we visited the WB Studios but my husband was not and he was very impressed from beginning to end. It was very special for me to see so many sets and props from the movies! This place is HUGE and doesn't seem to be missing anything - apart from the actors themselves. The staff are knowledgeable and you can tell they love to share their knowledge. You must try the Butterbeer icecream! My husband has now watched all the movies, and is currently reading the books so he'll appreciate it even more next visit. Can't wait to go back!

The coach was comfortable and clean. Our experience in Warner Bros Harry Potter Studio was fantastic! Better then expected and very enjoyable. The novelty wands are cheaper then expected. The coach back home was fantastic, Steve the coach driver was very friendly and happy, enjoyed the conversations and a very funny guy! Thanks for a great experience.

Went with my daughter who recently finished college. We both had a great time, and have had the urge to rewatch the Harry Potter films since we returned home. You will spend most of the day away from London with the commute, but if you're a fan, it will be worth the trip.

We took the bus from Vauxhall Bridge Road. Staff was very helpful. Our driver named Aston was extraordinary and he made our time in the bus a lot more pleasant.
It was a really good experience definitely we recommend the tour to everyone with Evan tours.

The props and tour itself is fantastic.
I was very disappointed however with our visit to the flying broomsticks today. It’s my sons birthday so we wanted to get the video and pictures of him flying. We had our pictures done and was told no need for a picture card just tell them 7020 and 7021 at the till. We went to the till and was told without a card they couldn’t do anything despite the couple next to me having the same issue and my sons pictures being up on the screen. After around 10 minutes of back and forthing they told me we would take new pictures. They made no attempt to do the video and didn’t even wait for my son to look at the camera. I had to settle with one picture of my son looking nearish to the camera as that was all they had time for. This was a huge dampener given it was so close to the start of the experience.

I booked Warner Bros. Studio Tour London - The Making of Harry Potter (with Return Transportation) through golden tours. Driver was right on time and contacted me in advance. Tour was worth visiting and pick up was smooth. Five stars to Golden Tours.

The experience is amazing!!!
As the fan of Harry Porter, I feel like walking in to the magic world. Really need to take around 4-5 hours to finish all spots. Also, must try the butter beer!!

I booked this tour for my wife who is a huge Harry Potter fan. I have never watched any of the movies but agreed to go with her on this tour. I was glad I did. You don't have to be a fan of the films to love this tour. Warner Bros did a fantastic job with all the exhibits, details, etc. We needed all 4 hours to see everything. Even though it was crowded, we were able to get many good pictures. Great souvenir shops and the food places are good also. A must visit for Harry Potter fans.

All I can say is WOW. Huge improvement from 6 years ago. Gringotts bank was fantastic. It was good to see the Hogwarts express, and the enchanted forest was a great new add on for us. The experience was amazing will go again.

Family of five with a mix of experience about the movies. It was AMAZING! The set and costume details were interesting. The on-site food options were good and reasonably-priced. We spent the whole day wandering through the exhibits.

We were so excited to visit. It didn't quite live up to the hype but was tons of fun. So glad we did it! 4 hours was plenty of time to see everything and still have time for lunch and a butterbeer. A definite must if you're a fan! Bus was on time and easy to find.

This was one the highlights for our London trip. The whole family loved the experience. Transportation from Evan Eavns tours was prompt and easy to find. We spent total 4 hours including lunch at HP tour.

My husband and I were on our honeymoon and had decided to do the Warner Bros. Studio tour with Evan Evans. I had been so looking forward to this tour that when I woke up the morning of I was quite excited. We arrived at the required location to check into the tour, did so, and waited. About 15 minutes after the bus was supposed to arrive to pick us up one turned up. Half the people waiting with us got on at which point that bus was filled to capacity. This left the rest of us waiting on the pavement wondering what on earth we were supposed to do. There was no communication from Evan Evans (The lady in the office never left her desk to let us know what was happening; if she even knew what was happening!) and no other bus had arrived to pick us up. Another bus eventually turned up about 10 minutes later at which point the other bus had long left for the studio.

So we eventually made it to the studio on the second bus (which was also filled to capacity) and we were told to be back at the bus by a certain time ready for departure. Fair enough. We were not given nearly enough time to see everything there was to see at the studio and my husband and I ended up rushing through the last part of the tour. Regardless we had had a great time (loved everything there was to see there) at the studio despite what had happened that morning with the buses..

We arrived back at our bus only to find it completely full. Apparently (for reasons unknown to us) two people from the first bus had not gotten on and were told that they could just get on our bus instead. That bus had already departed the studio. Our bus driver didn't seem to know what to do and eventually approached another bus driver from another tour to see if he could take us back instead. He couldn't and by this point I was getting very angry and very upset wondering how on earth we were supposed to get back to our hotel. To their credit both bus drivers did everything they could to help us and gave us instructions on how to get back which involved a local bus and a train. All of this at our own expense mind you.

I am absolutely disgusted that this happened. It ruined the whole day for me. I would never do a tour like this with Evan Evans again. In fact if it wasn't for two wonderful day trips with two wonderful tour guides with this same company I would never use them again full stop!

We used this tour company on the 10th December 2017 and were not happy with the service that the tour operator Evans Evans provided. There was lots of snow in London that day so we understood that there would be some delays but the service was still ridiculous!
To start with, we turned up on time at 10.30am and noticed people were already getting on the coach so we assumed that we would get straight on too. We asked the man in uniform who was stood there what we should do but he didn't speak to us. We asked him again as we thought he didn't understand us, he then shouted at us to get inside and wait with the rest of the people! He was completely rude to us and could have told us that to begin with (he turned out to be our driver for the day!).
Our tour left 20 minutes late as the first bus was full, then we drove around for half an hour once we were on the bus to go and pick up some people from a Hilton hotel even though our voucher clearly said that there would be no hotel pick-ups! They also allowed a woman from our tour to get off the bus twice and we had to wait a further 10 minutes each time on the road waiting for her to get back! This made us an hour late already and with all of the snow that day it took us another 2 hours to get to the Harry Potter tour!
With us getting there so late and having 3 hours for the tour, we had to then make our own way back to Euston as we had to catch the last train home to Liverpool and we weren't going to make it back with this tour company.
I would never use this tour company again.

Travelling from Australia, in town for a week in early August 2019. Booked Harry Potter tix online after WB site was sold out. Evan Evans accepted our booking and charged me in full for tickets. 48 hours later I receive an email to indicate they have no tickets available for the dates required, or indeed any dates within a week. Gotta love paying $800+ AUD for tickets the operator never had the right to sell. Evan Evans customer service team were of no help - the booking website just now still showing tickets available for the 6th August, even though no such tickets exist according to their own "customer service" operators. Was lucky enough to find tickets elsewhere - Golden Tours - albeit at higher cost. Avoid Evan Evans like the plague unless you like paying for tickets you'll never receive. Oh, and don't start me on the responsiveness once they realised they owed me a refund - amazingly I got immediate radio silence once it became clear they were in the wrong. Go elsewhere if you want the thing you actually paid for - I know, seems crazy, right? Appalling.

Please save your money and avoid this scam! We booked our tour through Evan Evans because all of the tickets directly from WB Studio were sold out.

When the bus left for WB Studio, it drove around and stopped twice to pick people up who did not board the bus on time. This was frustrating because this was at the expense of everyone who boarded the bus on time, and we wasted 40 minutes doing this before actually heading to WB Studio. In addition, our tickets clearly stated that there would be no other pick-up points.

We got to the studio almost two hours after first boarding the bus, and were handed a standard ticket. We were told which bus number to board for departure along with the departure time. The tour itself (which is completely separate from this company) was incredible! However the food is very mediocre so I would recommend bringing your own (you can eat your own food in the cafe, but not during the actual tour).

When we looked for our departure bus, there were no “services of a guest service assistant on departure from the Studio Tour” to help us find our bus. The bus matching the number and description we were told earlier was not a “luxury Mercedes coach” as promised by Evan Evans. It was a very old and dirty bus without WiFi, and the driver was very confused and did not even know what Evan Evans was, as they were expecting a different group to board. Multiple people from our original bus were confused and tried calling Evan Evans, but they were unable to give us further information. As this was the only bus that matched the description we were told earlier, everyone got on this bus because the driver said it was going to Victoria Station. The driver drove 30 minutes in the opposite direction before turning around and heading to Victoria Station, and when another passenger asked if we were going to Victoria Station (after discovering that we were going in the opposite direction) the bus driver did not answer her question.

We were completely ripped off by Evan Evans’ false advertising - avoid this company at all costs! If you are able to get admission tickets into the WB Studio Tour directly, use an alternative method of transport.

The tour of Harry Potter studio was fantastic, this is a negative review for Evan Evans Tours. They are a horrid company that is completely unorganized. The "luxury Air conditioned" bus was nothing more than a cramped coach bus that did not have working A/C. It was a gigantic rip off. My suggestion would be to save your money take the underground to the overground and then a quick easy bus ride to the studios rather than wasting your time with this joke of a company. Every negative thing someone has said about the tour company is true. Just do it all yourself and save money time and headache.

We booked this tour via Evan’s web site, payment get through, E- ticket and confirmation email received. Unfortunately on the day itself, when we arrive at Evan’s office, they told us that our booking has been cancelled due to fully booked. We didn’t plan anything for this day other than the tour, this cancellation just screw up our itinerary.

When I asked for refund, reception just told me to email their reservation instead of doing it for us.

Fine, after emailed to their reservation with the screen shoot of my credit card bill, their replied was “ you are not booked directly with Evan, pls contact third party agency for the refund”. Oh gosh!!! The credit card bill clearly shown that payment was paid to Evan, the E- ticket given by them with reference number attached. Why can’t their do some home work first before reply?

Anyway. In conclusion:
1. If it is fully booked, how come the web site still accept my booking and let the payment go through?

2. If it is fully booked after the payment go through, they should refund immediately instead of wait until we discovered and ask for it right?

3. If it is fully booked, why they still send us the E-ticket and confirmation email? Further more, one day before and one day after the tour, I can still received email from Evan for this booking. One is to remind us to meet at the pick up point on time and the other one is to provide feedback after the tour.

4. If I cancel the booking, I will ask for the refund. If you cancel it, am I right to say that you should process it for me instead of asking me to request myself? (poor customer service)

5. “Contact third party agency for the refund” - Online transaction clearly will show all the details; ref no, from who to whom, transaction date, amount etc. I can still get this replied from them. 😂

***I want to rate them 0, but there is no 0 available in the selection.

The studio tour was fantastic. Very well thought out and entertaining for our whole family. The "Luxury" tour bus ride from Evan Evans, not so much. It starts with a crowded and confusing waiting area. We were told to arrive 15 minutes early, then the tour left 10 minutes late. Not so much of a big deal, until we took a 30 minute detour to pick up a family at their hotel. The tour specifically states it is not door-to-door, you must meet at the Evans office. That again would not have been so bad if our tour driver had not made a bathroom and lunch stop along the way at a rest area for 20 minutes while the whole tour was left wondering what was going on. There was no Wi-Fi, as advertised and we were spoken to like children when told when and where to meet the bus to leave. All of these things individually are not a big deal, but when added together, with no apologies, made the tour a complete waste. Save yourself the trouble and take an Uber to the studios...you'll be much happier you did!

First of all -- the WB Studio was amazing and definitely worth going! My family was blown away by it all, especially my husband (who hasn't read the books or seen any of the movies). A very fun family adventure.

We booked through TripAdvisor for an Evans Evans round trip excursion -- family package (2 adults/ 2 youth). Once we arrived the day of the excursion, Evans Evans informed me that TripAdvisor had listed the youth tickets as "infants" and that we needed to pay the extra amount. I showed them the documentation from TripAdvisor listing the family package etc. and EvansEvans informed me that TripAdvisor does this trick a lot.

Shame on your TripAdvisor -- I thought you were supposed to be a "safer harbor" for travelers.

My husband and I and 2 friends travelled with Evans Evans to see the Making of Harry Potter sets. There were several things that were disappointing with the service we were provided by Evans and Evans.

Checking in and getting our tickets was simple at the front desk but shortly after waiting in the waiting room downstairs, were greeted by a young lady (who ended up being our leader for the day). She was very disorganised. Once we got onto the bus (after we had rudely been pushed the back of the line by other guests) we were informed we would be leaving later than expected because of a late customer.. that set the tone from the start as it meant there were no firm expectations from the company. Why should the people who have done the right thing and arrived on time have to wait for people who are disorganised and late. Sorry, but if you're not there on time, you should miss out.

The bus was clean but it would have been nice to have watched the Harry potter movie on the way seeing as it is a HARRY POTTER attraction..

When we arrived, our bus driver told us not to come back to the bus early as"its my break and it isnt my job to look after you on the bus during my break". It makes complete sense that you have non-existent time but the manner in which this information was presented was very unprofessional.

When we arrived we were told to stay seated on the bus until our leader returned with tickets. When she did, we had to reconfirm who we were (after giving her the same paperwork 3 times already). She then handed the tickets out and as the bus was full, some families were apart and this caused major disruption. We were sitting at the back of the bus so we were waiting for 20 minutes to get off the bus... right before we had to join a huge waiting line outside the display. Could the tickets not have been handed out when all of us were off the bus and in our groups?

The thing that was most displeasing was the behaviour of staff when we returned to the bus. We were instructed to be back by 2pm (which we were) amd we stood in front of the bus where both the leader and the bys driver could see us. They proceeded to sit in the warm bus while we stood in the cold until 2.20pm.

The bus ride was clean and we enjoyed harry potter world but next time we would have no hesitation in booking with the harry potter themed buses and will not reccomend Evans Evans to our travelling friends.

Hello, We did not book this with a tour company but did the planning and with reading other reviews in trip advisor. It was very easy.

Took the underground (subway) to Euston. Then took the Euston Train to Watford Junction(direct in 20 mins- depending upon the train schedule). Then took Warner's Bros bus ride from Junction to the studio.

As soon as I booked the Harry Potter tour (do this as soon as you know you are going to this tour to set the time and date you want) I booked the train ride.

Underground: very easy, there are many people at each station that can help you get to this location using this transportation.

I went on the train line web site and bought 2 tickets for Anytime travel for the date of the tour: going to and the return trip (Euston to Watford junction). This way, we didn't have a set time we had to be on the train and we didn't have a set time on when we had to leave the Harry Potter Tour and go back to London.

We ordered these online and had them mailed to our home in the US.

the bus from Watford to Warner's was right out side of the train station. Very well organized.

When I added up the total cost, saved approx $100.00 US. Plus, we had the Digital Guide. And you set the time, not someone else.

We were there (in the studio) for approx 6 hours. Since we knew we were not under a time schedule to get back on a tour bus, we were in no rush and just enjoyed the experience.

the experience at H. Potters was great. Learned about the making of the characters, had pictures taken, listened to people on the set of the movies (taped). It was a wonderful day. Very smooth. It was never to the point of too many people.

I do have a price list of the food, its average for the area.

Just a wonderful time, if you are a fan of Harry Potter !!!

Warner Bros tickets were sold out during US Thanksgiving, so we bought these super over-priced tickets. The two stars is for making last-minute tix available to Warner Bros. Studios, for which they can take zero credit. What it provides, besides tix to Warner Bros., is an inconvenient bus ride from Victoria Station in London to the Warner Bros .Studios which puts you on a precise schedule. In our case, the bus left the Warner Bros. lot seven minutes early. I called the tour to ask them to swing the bus back around, as it was still in sight and was several minutes before departure time, but operator rudely informed me that the bus couldn’t have left as it wasn’t 7 yet, and hung up. She didn’t pick up for the next 5 min. They knew I had two children in tow, one an infant. There was only a Premium Tours bus patiently waiting until 7 and local buses in the desolate, cold parking lot. Luckily my older child is a big HP fan and was delighted not to have to conform to the bus schedule. So we went back, browsed a bit more at our leisure, took the vastly cheaper, faster, more convenient public transit route for our hotel location. Moral of the story: buy your Warner Bros Studio tix directly waaaaay in advance so you can avoid relying on this service.

The review Brook F wrote almost exactly describes what my wife and I experienced. We booked 2 seats, we were charged, we received 2 tickets confirmed and had them printed out. Arriving at the office for our tour we were shocked to find that we weren't on their list. Come to find out they had sent another email that we didn't see stating that they didn't actually have availability for the tickets that were already sold and delivered to us. So today they said there was no way for us go on the tour today and we should have responded to their email. As their policy is to not offer refunds on the same day, they didn't agree to even offer a refund until my wife exchanged harsh words with them. So we are sitting here in the hotel very upset on the last day of our vacation, such a let down. Evan evans started sending other spam email after the initial booking and their followup email got mixed in with it and we missed it but if they were more considerate they should have either not given us tickets they couldn't uphold or tried harder to notify us of the problem. There was plenty of time between April and June where they could have tried to reach out again, instead they just held onto our money. I really hope that refund comes through in the next three days but regardless, this day for us is spoiled.

My wife and I visited London for a few days at the end of September. One of the things that my wife really wanted to see was the Making of Harry Potter exhibit at Warner Brothers studio so we tried to book tickets at the beginning of September. The only tickets that were available from the studio were for a late afternoon entry, but we were seeking a morning entry so we could head back to our hotel while it was still light outside. The only way we could obtain a morning ticket was to book a trip through a third party - in this case Evan Evans. We booked a trip for a 8:45 AM tour on Friday September 21, 2018 through Viator/TripAdvisor.

We subsequently learned that people felt rushed by the tour companies and we wanted to take our time visiting the studio, so on Sept 3 I contacted Evan Evans via email to ask how long we were allowed to stay at the studio on their tour. I received a response that they would reply shortly, but never received a reply.

On September 8, I found that some morning tickets became available at Warner Brothers studio, so I purchased tickets for my wife and I, and cancelled the Evan Evans tour at 3:40 pm CST on 9/8/18 through viator/TripAdvisor. Once cancelled, I didn't think about the Evan Evans tour again until by credit card was billed for $219 for the tour. As it turns out, even though I had cancelled the Evan Evans tour and we never went on it - TripAdvisor did not process the cancellation and I was stuck with the charge.

This is not an indictment of Evan Evans tours - or TripAdvisor for that matter. I am just frustrated that the cancellation was not processed and I was stuck with paying for a tour that I never went on.

Just be extra careful with TripAdvisor cancellations and bookings! Document. Document. Document.
The displays were excellent and gave a good insight into the films. However, the price of food, drinks and souvenirs is eye-watering.

I’m reviewing the Evans & Evans element of this package and excluding the Harry Potter tour itself (will review that separately, it was good).

We arrived and jumped on the bus, yeh, it’s a nice bus, but it just takes you to WB Studio & back to the original location; there is no entertainment provided on the bus, or any kind of commentary on the way - some hints or tips about the attraction would be nice, or some info on places we passed on the way out of London & would have earned this a better rating.

Luckily, we made good time to WB, so there weren’t any delays getting in. I can understand however that if traffic was bad you could get there late and be caught in the queues.

Because we got in quickly, we had plenty of time, however 4 hours may not be long enough if you’re travelling with Kids or have mobility constraints. Could be better to just get your own public transport & book well in advance.

Just to be clear, this isn’t a Tour, it’s pretty much a bus ride with an entry ticket (because as others have said, the shysters buy all the tickets out, so you have to buy them through the Tour company). Best to work out if tickets are available from the official website, then what the public transport costs would be from your location.

Side note - we booked this only a month or so before travelling, so there were not many other options available at the time.

We visited London after Christmas a stayed until January 4th. There was no chance to get tickets during this period. I was trying at all web sites, but I was not successful. So I wrote directly to Evan Evans and ask them to inform me, if there will be some tickets free again. And two days before our departure to London I received the email with information that tickets are available!!! This was the biggest Christmas gift for our kids.
We did good decision that we travel with agency, as there were no worries with transport from London to studios and back. More than four hours for studios is enough for all Harry Potter fans.
and the studios themselves are really worth to see!

First things first, the Studio experience was awesome and the people at EE in London were very polite and the waiting facilities were good. Perhaps the loo should get fixed though; we had to go across to road to take a leak.
We were checked in and handed our tickets to get on the bus, still good so far.
But then things started to go south somewhat, as it seemed there were too many people on board the bus all of a sudden. I have no idea how, but apparently some folks got left at the sidewalk as the rest of us took off toward Watford.
On our way there, things were nice and comfy, until the driver decided to pull into a gas station, where he left us for 10 minutes. We were all looking at each other somewhat confused, but luckily he returned and we got back on the road.
At the studio we were greeted by our host, who gave a very short briefing, emphasizing the words .. "DO NOT BE LATE". They really mean it .. The bus left at 18:00 on the dot. Now, I can't be sure, but it felt like we had several rows of empty seats on the way back that we had occupied going to the Studio, but I digress.
Just like other reviews have mentioned, we were also kept outside in the cold because we came out before 17:45, and the bus driver got very defensive (that's putting it mildly) when comments were made to the fact that it was cold outside.
Whereas the trip to the studio was very comfy, the trip back sure wasn't. There was no question in my mind that the driver just wanted to get home, and I for one, am VERY happy the bus had seat belts, because dear lord, I needed it. I have never been so happy to get off a bus as I was when we finally made it to Victoria station.

So to sum up, the experience is AWESOME, but please EE, take care and screen your drivers just a little bit better, yea?

So to be fair -

1. We left exactly on time
2. Great organization, easy to find, great bus

Not so great -

1. We were on 1pm tour and departure back from Warner brother studios was at 7!!!! That’s way more time than we needed and we’d be missing our evening show ( I saw this info nowhere but maybe just me), but nice lady who met us there to hand out tickets ( that’s all that’s provided besides the bus) offered for us to take earlier bus.

Well driver of that bus was super rude and made us leave the bus telling us it was full ( even though it was a few min before departure and obviously seats left). Then as we were looking for alternatives ( which are by the way pretty simple and wouldn’t take any longer via train + bus), he came chasing us down and told us we can get on. Was unpleasant.

2. There were multiple confused people on that bus expecting to be dropped off somewhere , I guess like prior reviewer parent. They kept walking up to the driver and he was supremely rude literally yelling at them telling to go back sit
Down and that he will only stop at Victoria station (it sounds like they picked up other places so people naturally expected similar so not sure why the anger)..

.

I loved every bit of WB Studios. I am a huge Harry Potter fan. It was great seeing everything and hearing how they made some parts of the movie. I would go here again but probably without the tour company. Nobody from the company goes with you and the bus is ok at best. If you are a Harry Potter fan and don't want to do the leg work yourself, then this a tour for you.

Really bad experience. Advertise a service and then after paying for it tell you it no longer exists and to contact someone else to get your money back. Really Unhelpful. Would not reccommend booking Harry Potter tour with Evans Evans tours

BE CAREFUL WITH THIS COMPANY!!
They're not serious. Came from the other side of the world to take this tour, and they canceled my reservation saying it was because of low people in the tour. That sucks, i was waiting to take the tour (main reason why I went to London), and they ruined my vacations.

Now I dont have my money, I don't have any reservation, but 2 days where I don't know what the hell I'm going to do.

Purchased this tour for me and my son when visiting London. Arrived at Evan Evans office for the coach (bus) trip to the studio at about 7:15am and on the road a little after 8am.

You are paying Evan Evans to purchase your tickets and provide transportation to the studio. There is no commentary on the bus ride.

We finished the studio tour and lunch about 1 1/2 hours before the Evan Evans bus was scheduled to depart, so we took the free shuttle to the Watford train station and caught the Northern Rail line back to Euston Station in London. Train ride is about 30 minutes vs. more than an hour on the bus. We transferred to the Victoria Line, and walked through the Belgrave neighborhood and were browsing the Victoria and Albert Museum before the bus was even scheduled to depart the studio!

For a stress free trip, certainly purchase this tour with Evan Evans. The fee for the coach trip and tickets is quite fair. However, if you really want to keep your own schedule, you can easily take the train to Watford and buy your tickets at the studio.

Writing this review in advance of a visit to Harry Potter studios. We were planning a trip to celebrate our Potter mad son’s birthday this Sunday but sadly the direct tickets with WB studios weren’t available so we searched online and found availability with Evans & Evans. We live close to the studios so a trip into London to then get a bus out again seemed crazy. After checking with Get Your Guide, they confirmed that we could book the tour with Evans and Evans (paying full price of course!) but could go straight to the studios rather than taking the coach. This was very expensive however we kept a little boy and his sister very happy! Imagine our disappointment when we learned that Evans & Evans we’re now insisting that the only way we could go was on the coach, meaning hours journeying into London, to then spend a further 2 hours on a coach out again to the studios. Clearly this isn’t an option so we have ruined a birthday and two hugely disappointed children. Surely it isn’t beyond the realms of possibility to allow people to travel independently to the studios? And surely this could have been correctly advised upon so we could have sought an alternative operator. Now everything is sold out.

My husband and I went with our 17yo son who grew up with the HP books and movies, he spent many an hour running round the garden with a drawn on scar, glasses and a homemade broomstick or sword of Gryffindor.

We had an absolutely fabulous day, arriving at 11.45 and we left 6 hours later, we didn’t expect to spend so long. The attention to detail was amazing and it’s these details that made the movies a huge success.

We will definitely visit again.

Visited HP Warner Bros studio and chose to use Evan Evans Tour as getting there on your own can be tricky.
Bus driver, Mike, was great! Hearing him talking about London brought many smiles and laughs.
We were at the studio a bit early so in the end we had 4.5h before we needed to be back at the bus. We were done with the whole tour withing 2.5 hours and needed to sit 2 hours in the studio's cafe to wait for the departure time.
I don;t think anyone needs that much time unless there are big queues to get in.

Studio itself - fantastic!

We travelled as a family of 4 to see all things Harry Potter. Everything was great... except we did not have enough time. We had to rush in the end to make it back to bus on time. Easily tour could have been for 30mins to 1 hr longer.

I have no words to describe how amazing this attraction is. As a Harry Potter Mad 13 year old, I can say that there is plenty for people of all ages to do! I won’t tell you much because I don’t want to spoil the secret, but, take my word, it is DEFINITELY worth the money.

Amazing experience for those who love the wizarding world. By yourself you need a good 3 hours. In a group longer. Take extra money for green screen experiences Loved it and would do it again. A must while in London

First I have to say, it was AWESOME. The sets, costumes, props, posters, words, wands, train, everything. It is really a lot to take in. I felt like I was walking sacred halls and was overwhelmed with the details. I think 4 hours is enough time, however, never being there before, I wanted to just stand and absorb it all, but I kept pushing myself to go go go, I didn't want to be left behind!. That part sucked! I could have spent more time in some areas. Once you go thru one area, you can't really go back, so be sure you take it all in and be sure you saw everything you wanted in that area. Some areas do not have doors, so you can walk back. Some have "workers" standing guard, so you can't go back. I can't emphasis enough the details and how intricate this stuff is!
The last corner of the "tour" is where the model of Hogwarts grounds. I entered before my daughter and was awe struck, mouth dropped, stars in my eyes, I wish I has my camera ready to get her face when she rounded that corner. DO IT FOR YOUR HARRY POTTER NERD, they will love you forever!!! Have that camera ready!
The Evans and Evans part of this was not overwhelming - we met in a small office area, with one bathroom and 45 ppl - so there was a line, ppl getting ready for the hr + drive, if you hit traffic. No toilet on the bus.

The trip with Evan Evans tour is a great choice, the driver Mark is amazing, he has been an unexpected guide during the trip to the studios, talking us about the peculiarity of the places we were crossing around London.
The Harry Potter studio is a must if you are a true fan. I would definitely recommend the tour and I would do it again in occasion of a future visit to London.

I enjoyed the studio tour, but the experience with Evan Evans left a sour taste in my mouth. The "luxury" coach was 20 minutes late to the pickup, then once we got on we didn't leave the city of London for another hour and a half because the bus stopped to pick up other passengers about three times throughout the city. This caused the entire trip to the studio to take TWO AND A HALF HOURS. It was extremely frustrating. Plus, the "luxury" coach is just a bus.
Absolutely BRILLIANT only downside is on the main Warner Bros, website does not mention anything about paying for the bus ride

You should understand that this tour simply provides comfortable shuttle transportation to and from the Harry Potter studios and guaranteed tickets for entry. That said, we received excellent service from Evans Tours. We traveled to and from the studios in clean, new and comfortable coaches! We did not have to worry about a thing except for enjoying our day at the studio.

About the studio, unless you really want to spend significant amounts of time mulling over every movie prop, the 4 hour tour is sufficient to see the whole studio. More than that and you may find yourself waiting around for a few hours for the return shuttle. We did the 4 hour tour and it was just right!

Easy and comfortable bus out to the studios. Was skeptical if studios were worth it - but all very impressive and kids thought the visit was the highlight of our trip. Money well spent. Happy we took the bus and didn't have to mess around with public transportation.

You have to go to this tour the studios are amazing
Everything about Harry Potter movies is there the place is amazing loved loved it

Overall this was a great experience. It was nice not having to worry about transportation to or from the studio being from a different country and the studio being an hour from London. The check in process was smooth, nice buses and relaxing ride. The only thing is I wish there was a little extra time st the studio. There is so much to see and explore but we were constantly watching the clock to make sure we wouldn’t miss the bus back and we ended up finishing an hour early and you can’t go back through. But overall great experience. Would book again!

We were hesitating for the different tours but we choose this one and we are happy to. It was very well organised.

The instruction we got before coming were very precise. They were always on time and on schedule.

we quite appreciated the first part of the journey with the funny presentation by the guide inside the bus.

nothing to complain, you can go for it!

My boyfriend and I thoroughly enjoyed our day at the Warner Bros Studio with Evan Evans Tours. The pickup location and bus were clean, the staff were friendly, and the timing that they laid out for us (30 min for check-in, 1 hour bus ride there, 4 hours of time at the studio, and 1 hour bus ride back) was perfect. They even provided clear instructions for how to return to London if people missed the return bus, whether intentionally or accidentally. The guide on the way to the studio gave good information and was very entertaining (he didn't talk the whole hour, just the first 5 or 10 min and the last 5 min or so). The bus was comfortable - it was a hot day and everyone had to blast the AC for the whole ride, but the bus managed to keep up.

The actual studio tour was so much fun. There were so many sets, costumes, and other props from the actual filming. It was really cool just being on location. My boyfriend was surprised at how much work was put into the film - I guess he thought so much more of the films was CGI'ed. The models were very impressive. My favorite part of the whole tour was how many interactive experiences there were and how many times you could incorporate yourself into the Harry Potter world. It's a great tour for anyone who has connected with the Harry Potter franchise.

Book early, as it sells out quickly! Worthwhile for anyone loving the series - young or old! Easy to find Evan Evans Tours and convenient to let them drive. No Wi-Fi on the bus, so be aware, but air conditioned and comfortable. Don't expect the same food and drinks as at Universal, which is better. However, they do have butterbeer.

Checking in process is organized. They have a waiting room; someone will announce that registration is opening and 1 person from each party will collect the wrist bands. The wrist bands indicate what time your bus is going to be ready to board coming back and what time it will absolutely leave. You know they are being serious about this because they also give you a sealed envelope containing instructions on how to go home on your own in case you miss the bus (avoid if you can, it takes a shuttle and two train rides - but if you fall in love with the place and need more time then hey - to each their own). Go to the bathroom when you are there.

Bus is very comfortable - I knocked out pretty quick.

Harry Potter is amazing - go as a fan. The people who go and are done in 2 hours are not real fans. This is not a theme park - there are no roller coasters or anything like that. There are literal sets and props from the movie. Other than that, there are interactive activities like: being able to do a simulated flying video on a broomstick, doing a practice wand/spell class, picture opps sitting inside the train to Hogwarts, etc. Beware of picture prices: one print was 14 GBP, the broomstick video cost 20GBP. I bought 4 pictures and got a discount to 10GBP each.

There’s a cafeteria halfway through. Butterbeer was like 4GBP (not in a special commemorative cup), burgers with chips at 9GBP. They also had sandwiches (prepackaged) at about 6 GBP.

There’s a large store at the end. Out in the lobby there’s a cafe too. I dont know how this happened but they ran out of ice cream at like 4pm.

The Studios continue to expand so I think it’s worth going back. My cousin came with us (her 4th time) and she said there were new things she’d never seen before.

You really only have 4 hours to do everything. For me, I would gauge that 5.5 to 6 hours would have been just right. Evan Evans, you should offer a longer tour option. We did about half of the interactive stuff, spent time in the 1st half, had a quick lunch, and literally just zoomed through the last half. We were definitely rushing through the gift shop for fear of missing the bus. So spend time wisely! have a game plan.

You dont get dropped off back at the storefront. There are two dropoffs: 1 before victoria station, and another right outside victoria station.

Dear Evan Evans Tours,
this attraction could have gotten an Excellent, however the bus driver on the way back was absolutely ignorant and rude. He had my daughter in tears before even boarding the bus back to London. She was holding a take-out cup with COLD water and he assumed that she was drinking coffee. I told him she was not...He again assumed that I was lying and told me that obviously I can't ready because the rules are on the website...he went on and on about it. Such an unnecessary upset. Even if we had a hot beverage, there is a way to talk to people in a respectful way and remind them of the rules. I do it on a daily basis as a flight attendant. Otherwise the attraction was fabulous, we had plenty of time to see all the exhibits. Leaving in the morning was a bit confusing because we had to stand in line to get our wristbands. The bus was almost full and we were told that we may have to take the 1 pm one. That didn't make sense to me since we booked the 1030...anyway I ask you to take to the bus company because it reflects badly on you as a tour company. He was also rude to other passengers not just us...

BOOK AHEAD OF TIME!! You will not be able to purchase tickets at the gate. Transportation to and from the studio is convenient and easy from the London Underground. Bring cash for the 10 minute bus ride to the studio from Watford Junction Station (£2.50 per visitor).

We love the HP books and movies, and the studio tour was an excellent way to see some of the behind-the-scenes magic of the series. Plan on spending 3-4 hours at the studio, and give yourself an extra hour and a half (one way) for transportation.

Finally, you CANNOT buy “butter beer” outside the exhibit, only at the Backlot Cafe about halfway through the tour. However, there are additional dining options outside the exhibit.

It was thrilling to see the sets used in the Harry Potter films. I particularly liked the Gryffindor common room where so many important scenes take place and the dining hall. Of course the dining hall is made to look larger on film than it looks in the set, but that did not dampen my enthusiasm. Many of the costumes and masks, for non-wizard characters, are on display. I made a point to have a Butterbeer and to take a photograph of myself pushing a luggage trolley through the 9 3/4 wall at the train station. And of course there's a huge and wonderful gift shop at the end. The bus service was excellent; the stay provided time for a leisurely tour.
The staff was very welcoming and the bus was clean! The bus trip to the tour was comfortable as well! Professional! Would recommend

If you are a Harry Potter fan, I strongly recommend a visit to the Warner Brothers Studios. After reading that these tours sell-out, we booked our tour two months in advance. Online booking was quick and easy. We met near Victoria Station in London and we boarded a shuttle. During the trip, in a double-decker bus, we watched Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone. We toured the studios on our own. I was amazed to see the actual props and costumes used in the filming of the movies. There were a few features/displays that had long lines. I don't want to say what these features are, but they were popular, especially with kids. We skipped those lines and in doing so, it took us about two hours to go through the entire studio. About midway through our experience, we came across the Backlot Cafe, where we sampled butterbeer ice cream. It was delicious. During the shuttle ride back to central London, we watched Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets. Bring your camera. Photographs are allowed. This tour is for both young and old fans of Harry Potter.

Driver had a great personality but the ride felt quite impersonal.
No information whatsover given about the journey, duration of the tour, what to expect.

Once we got to the studio, whoever was the welcoming host did a VERY poor job:
lad did not even wait for everyone to get out of the coach and started giving instructions (especially important details such as what time to regroup to leave). When someone asked if he could repeat the instructions, the request was pretty much ignored.

On the way back, no information about drop-off points. Driver pretty much pulled off at locations other passengers request. Mates and I were at a total loss as to where we were meant to get off board.

Overall - Warner Bros studio itself was great, but Evan Evans Tours was a VERY confusing and frustrating trip to get to and back from there.

I sent my 17-year old son on this trip. Since I sent him on his own, I wrote several mails to Evans Evans to make sure that everything was in order and received confirming answer mails. The pick-up point was at the Original Visitor Center close to our hotel and I assumed that he would return there with the coach in the afternoon. I walked him there, made sure that he got on the coach and showed him how to return to our hotel (a 5 min. walk). On his way back, the heard that the coach only goes to Victoria Station (30 min travel from our hotel) and not to where he was picked up. I did not receive any information about this, not by the personnel answering my mails or by the guide who accompanied the coach in the morning. We live in a small city abroad and my son is not at all familiar with London or the transport system there. I called the office and while the operator agreed that a mistake had been made by them and was empathetic, he didn't make any effort whatsoever to solve it. I asked if they could at least pay the taxi for him from Victoria to our hotel and he said there was no such possibility. I had to leave the walking tour I was on and rush to Victoria station to get him. In my opinion, it was very irresponsible by the tour operators and guide that I was in contact with not to give me the information that my son would not be returned to the pick-up point. I chose Evans Evans even though they were more expensive than other identical tours because I received the impression that they were more reliable but I was very disappointed.

I can't begin to express how happy we were with this tour and company! First, we had a top-notch day. The accommodations to and from the studio were fabulous. The studio itself was beyond impressive and far exceeded our family's expectations! However, it was EVAN EVANS TOURS who we must thank profusely! On our return from this amazing day, my 13 year old son left his jacket and phone on the bus. Discovering this back at our hotel, we made a call to Evan Evans with very little hope. We are so grateful Elizabeth answered the phone. To say this employee went above and beyond is putting it mildly. She tracked down the bus driver and bus. He located the items and returned them to the office the next day. Unfortunately, we flew back to the USA about an hour before the phone/jacket were back in the office. A few phone calls later, and Elizabeth had our items mailed via Royal Mail right to our home in South Carolina. I never thought we would see that phone again, but it arrived today! Liam was also helpful during some calls. Seriously, we are so impressed by the actions taken to return our items. Take this tour because it was GREAT, but know that the employees of Evan Evans are first-class. THANK YOU!

To be far, service was delivered to the description.

However, having gone through the experience, I wonder whether I would re iterate
- luxury bus is a regular Mercedes coach (no toilet for instance)

- departure is from Victoria station (south) to go to the north of London. So the trip is 1 hour but includes traffic jams. Train departs from north part of the London (Euston statin close to Saint Pancras) and takes 20 minutes to reach Watford Junction station (you have to go to the Euston station and use the Warner Bros shuttles (billed return according to website) between station and studio. So more complex but could be more convenient is you stay in the northern part of London

- the most uncomfortable aspect for me is the 4 hour stay there. When arriving to the office AND when stepping into the bus, we were told that we must be on time, otherwise bus would depart without us and it would be up to us to manage (and fund) our return to London. And indeed when arriving there, driver gave us exactly 4 hours 15 minutes between the moment when he opened the door of the bus (better seat in the front) and the time he would depart. And he really departed on time, no people counting what so ever having been done.

Actually the visit is supposed to last 3.5 hours. So we started the visit have a constant eye on the watch whilst trying to let kids appreciate but keeping momentum in the tour.

Eventually we achieved to comply with the timing, taking no break, listening only to the main explanations in the audio guide, not queuing at the activities. We could wander gently in the shop at the end. If we would have needed to include lunch or kids would have been younger (diaper change, sudden angers, ...) , it would have been a challenge.

So service delivered but the offer could benefit from being revisited and price adjusted

Makes you realize how much funding this movie had xD
The Great Hall was awesome, it's so much smaller than you'd think! Loads of props and explanations of how things worked. The gift store was expensive, but so's everything in the area. It was definitely one of the best things I did this trip!

Excellent tour!! My family and I attended this excursion on 2/17/2018 and loved every minute of the experience. The bus arrived at our hotel on time, very organized with a speedy check-in, and departed the studios on time as well.

Can't miss tour if you are a fan of the Harry Potter book and film series. Highly recommended!!
Super nice visit due to covid situation It was not full of people but we expected to see more magic tricks. Like movings pictures
Very nice tour operator. The bus was confortable and our driver Steve was awesome. Excelent service, highly recommended. For sure will use again if back in London.

I have only seen a couple of the Harry Potter movies, but my kids are huge fans, so they were dying to go. I was pleasantly surprised, lots of cool props to see from the movies. Many great spots for pictures too. The food is pretty good there, and reasonably priced. It was definitely a highlight of their trip.

Not that we need to tell you to visit, but if you have the opportunity don’t miss it. Evans & Evans was a fine transport. Nice to let others do the driving. We initially wondered how we would spend all the time but if you take the time to experience each exhibit you can actually run out of time. Really fun to see how things were made.

Harry Potter Studio Tour itself was fantastic and our family enjoyed every minute of it. We booked this tour through Evans because we wanted hassle free transport to and from the studios. BUT they left us and approximately 10 other people stranded in the cold and wet and in a foreign country with two children. It was specific that boarding the coach was at 2:20 and departure was at 2:30. They were gone before 2:20. We are now out of pocket for travel expenses to return to London plus an extra two hours of our time. We will not be using Evans again. If I could give less stars I would.

We waited 30 minutes just to get our tickets. The queue of hundred people standing to get tickets. We have not been told that we cant have food or drink on the bus until we actually reached it. Man on the bus had a very bad attitude towards the customers. We wouldn't recommend this service at all. The Warner Bros Harry Potter Studio was great and worth going but maybe with another company.

First of all I'm not a HP fan, I only watched the films (all of them) so let's just say I might not appreciate the tour. I genuinely think the tour was good though, it gave you a lot of back ground info of the movie with interviews and vids. The FX, sets design and other creative departments is something to truly admired. The staff were very friendly and smiley (very strange to see if you live in London) and genuinely seem to wanna be there (imagine going to the Lego shop and their staff).

But the bad side I found the tour was how much they trying to milk your money. OK I am also lucky enough not have to pay for a ticket, but wow I can't imagine being a parent there! Beside the obvious cost of the tour, things inside are so expensive. I meant come on? £4 for a butter beer served in a sh1tty plastic cup? If you like one where you like to keep the cup I think is £6.50/7. SPOILER alert, butter beer practically taste like root beer with some cream on top, seriously I think max £3 will do and that's already on the pricey side (I paid 10EUR for water in Ibiza and I think is worth it as they don't open all year long). I didn't bother looking at their food selection, but it seems it's only burgars and very unhealthy food. Being a tour where there a lot of children and perhaps over tired and poor parents (after paying for tickets) the least they can do is serve some healthy and well priced food. I think a burgar meal there is around £10 and no one seems to be enjoying what they were eating.

On the bus they tell you to take as many photos as you like and make sure to use their hashtag. Free marketing there for them and I feel quite bad if I have kids as they gets drummed in with all those commercialised rubbish.

The gift shop is almost like robbery for parents or true fans (is massive), it makes the Harrods gift shop looks cheap. I meant £50 for a poorly made sweatshirts? £35 for a wand? The quality is not great, is almost like going to Primark but with Harry Potter theme on it, is truly disappointing.

I can appreciate they have a unique position where the "brand" have possession of heart strings on so many children and fans, but I think they also need to be a bit more responsible of how they treat and pay back their fans and customers.

Again the staff were great and I can't say more on how lovely they are.

It was beyond expectations. The office was easy to find, the check-in & waiting area inside were comfortable on a cold day. The bus left on time and dropped us of 1 minute away from the entrance.

The tickets (got them at the office) were checked and 5 minutes later our journey continued inside. Not going to spoil anything from the tour itself, but it’s amazing and really worth the price.

The bus drove back on time and dropped us of at Victoria station where we took the underground.

Awesome day. Thanks Evan Evans!

From the moment we arrived our family was impressed with the friendliness of all the staff. The studios were very impressive and the craftsmanship of all the original sets could not have been surpassed. The tour was comprehensive and exceptionally well organised. Having spent the whole day at the Studios we could easily have spent many more hours as there was so much to see and admire.

Impressive set which took the entire day to travel to and visit.

About an hour out by coach

The tours are by timings indicated on your ticket

There was a student group before us so it was quite some queue but the wait was manageable

Inside, the butterbeer drink and ice cream were superb! Worth the queue which was about 15mins.

If you are a HP fan, it’s a must visit
If you aren’t, the creativity and magnitude of this studio will also impress

The retail store has lots of merchandise- too much so parents, beware!

I have the feeling this is a cheat: the company EvansEvans buys all the tickets of the WB so that we can not buy the tickets directly to the studio (they are all sold out for months), and then resells them for the double price.
Ok, they bring us there. But we could have traveled by train. And we came back to London by train on our own, not with EvanEvans, since they would have picked up us only 4 hours later, which was not enough for us.

If you were not a Harry Potter fan before you went on this tour, you will be after you leave. There is so much to see including costumes, sets, props, etc. I felt like a was transported to Hogwarts. You can even get some butterbeer, which tastes like caramel.

We took an afternoon tour 1pm with Evan Evans to the Warners Brothers Studio. It was very punctual and easy. We boarded luxury coach and had a smooth ride. The actual Studio is excellent and has everything you can imagine in regards to Harry Potter. We ate on site and completed the tour with a little time for shopping. The lines are long at the store but we were able to get what we wanted. If you really want to shop with ample time you will have to go through the studio a bit faster as to allow more time. Other than a crowded gift shop the tour was very good and we enjoyed it. There will be a lot of families and students at this site.
Wonderful studio everything was clean and professional. I know it was called a behind the scenes tour.

Just the lunch Who was extremely bad, just look the picture, I've been disrespected for my vegan menu who was served with meat and for replacing thos mistake, I had thos s..t, and they don't care ! Of course !
Fortunately the studio is wonderful ! It's a interesting art of work. but I've been disappointed for the rest of the visit because the worst is the visitors who shake up you !
Being from out of town we wanted an easy way to get to Harry potter studio tour. Easy location to get to for departure and it was great to know you had an easy and sure way to get there.

Well worth the money, it was nice not to have to worry about finding our way there. Our tour bus driver kept us entertained on the way there and back with loads of historical facts about London and even took us past some places we probably wouldn’t have seen on our own.
HP tour was phenomenal. It felt like it was real. It is amazing to see the amount of work and people that goes into making a movie like this. I thoroughly enjoyed it and so did my husband. (I told him he HAS to go with me 😉). And... you have to have a butterbeer. So tasty!
We had an amazing time there is so much to see and do there. Four hours for us wasn’t really long enough but I would still recommend to go
